papers.title: Euler: Towards Human-Centered Multi-Agent Mathematical Discovery
papers.translated_title: Euler: Towards Human-Centered Multi-Agent Mathematical Discovery
papers.author: Qiuyu Chen
papers.summary: Mathematical research drives scientific discovery, and recent advances in AI for mathematics have shown that language-model agents can solve challenging problems and develop substantial mathematical proofs. Yet much of today's AI-for-mathematics work centers on obtaining a final answer. This emphasis leaves the exploration behind a result difficult for researchers to understand, while long-running investigations face fragmented context and the risk of unsupported claims propagating across reasoning steps. We present Euler, a human-centered mathematical research system built around a shared, structured representation of the research process. Euler organizes mathematical statements, assumptions, proof dependencies, alternative approaches, failed attempts, and verification evidence into connected research graphs. This representation allows researchers to trace how results are developed and supplies agents with persistent, task-relevant knowledge for planning, collaboration, and verification across sessions. Researchers can also select a graph node linked to a saved team state, revisit the agents' earlier reasoning, and explore alternative directions through continued interaction. We illustrate Euler's capabilities through three mathematical research case studies and describe the implemented system and its software validation.

papers.title: When Extremists Enter LLM Societies: Investigating Extreme Behavior in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.translated_title: When Extremists Enter LLM Societies: Investigating Extreme Behavior in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.author: Guo Chen
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly serve as computational actors in multi-agent social simulations. While existing work emphasizes representative personas and average-case behavior, social science shows that persistent tail actors can disproportionately shape collective dynamics. We study this regularity in controlled LLM-based multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS). In these systems, such actors cannot be reduced to fixed scalar states: prompts, natural-language histories, and backbone generation mediate their behavior and influence. We first analyzed three properties of extremists in sociology and model the LLM extremist based on LLM-native perspective. We introduce EXAM, an EXtremist Agent Modeling framework that capable of configuring extremist agents for specific tasks and precisely controlling their population proportion, spatial distribution, interaction protocols, and measurement interfaces. Across four scenarios: congressional election, financial crisis, epidemic public opinion, and iterated prisoner's dilemma, we observe that small persistent tail groups produce measurable, backbone- and scenario-dependent collective shifts. EXAM shows how this social-science regularity manifests through language-mediated mechanisms specific to LLM-based social simulation.

papers.title: On the Optimisation Landscape of Overparameterised Weighted MMD
papers.translated_title: On the Optimisation Landscape of Overparameterised Weighted MMD
papers.author: Tharrshann Jayan Logarajah
papers.summary: We study the optimisation landscape of the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) over weighted atomic measures. For the one-dimensional Gaussian kernel, we show that, for any compactly supported target distribution, sufficiently many particles ensure that every local minimum has arbitrarily small MMD. Moreover, any stationary point whose MMD remains bounded away from zero is unstable under an unweighted gradient flow over the particle locations. These results hold both when the weights are constrained to the simplex, and when they are unconstrained but optimised at each step. When the target is itself finitely supported, we further strengthen this result: beyond an explicit particle threshold, there are no spurious local minima, and every spurious stationary point is unstable. To our knowledge, these are the first finite-particle overparameterisation guarantees of their kind for weighted MMD optimisation.

papers.title: Text-Informed Training Data Filtering for Enhanced Virtual Flow Meter Performance
papers.translated_title: Text-Informed Training Data Filtering for Enhanced Virtual Flow Meter Performance
papers.author: Kristoffer Hjelmen Nesland
papers.summary: In sectors such as energy, aquaculture and chemical processing, the effectiveness of both mechanistic and data-driven models is frequently limited by poor-quality training data, which obscures underlying physical laws and degrades predictive accuracy. Such quality issues commonly manifest as anomalies in the dataset, ranging from sensor faults to process upsets and incorrect operator inputs. While traditional rule-based filtering can remove a subset of the anomalies, it is unable to leverage contextual information stored as unstructured text, such as engineer comments and operational logs that explain under what conditions the data was collected. We propose a text-informed data filtering method that leverages large language models (LLMs) to integrate unstructured operational data with tabular sensor data. The method consists of two steps: (1) contextual anomaly detection by reasoning over both data modalities, and (2) generation of a binary mask that is applied to filter the training dataset for model development. To investigate the potential benefit, a steady-state soft-sensor regression model, namely a virtual flow meter that estimates well flow rates, is used as the downstream evaluation target. Experiments on a synthetic oil and gas dataset show improved model performance compared to traditional rule-based filtering. Ablation studies show that textual operator comments can provide filtering-relevant signals beyond sensor data alone, with the multimodal approach reducing downstream MAPE from 7.1% to 5.4% relative to sensor-only filtering. This work demonstrates that integrating unstructured operational knowledge with sensor data through LLMs can improve data quality for industrial machine learning applications, offering a scalable alternative to manual data curation.

papers.title: OmniPoser: Flexible Human Motion Recovery in the Wild with Masked Flow Matching
papers.translated_title: OmniPoser: Flexible Human Motion Recovery in the Wild with Masked Flow Matching
papers.author: Minghao Liu
papers.summary: Recovering 3D human motion from sparse wearable sensors is challenging due to the inherent noise, occlusion, and instability of real-world tracking signals. Existing approaches are restricted to fixed sensor configurations and, when built on diffusion models, are computationally prohibitive for real-time deployment. We propose OmniPoser, a universal framework that recovers full-body SMPL motion from a flexible combination of heterogeneous inputs, such as 3D keypoints, sparse IMU rotations, head-mounted 6-DoF poses, or any subset thereof, within a single model. OmniPoser introduces a cross-modal masking mechanism paired with a Masked Conditioning Encoder, enabling one architecture to incorporate diverse sensor configurations through a masked design. A decoupled dual-stream generative backbone generates complete motion via Conditional Flow Matching, requiring only a single ODE integration step at inference. Across three settings and seven benchmarks, including in-the-wild Nymeria and Ego-Exo4D datasets, OmniPoser performs on par with state-of-the-art methods while running at over 700 FPS. The project page is available at https://jamesbridgewater51.github.io/omniposer-eccv/.

papers.title: Lost in the Fallback: How Reliably Do Typed Decision Models Use Fallback Options?
papers.translated_title: Lost in the Fallback: How Reliably Do Typed Decision Models Use Fallback Options?
papers.author: Yuanbo Xie
papers.summary: Typed decision models (TDMs) are increasingly used in applications such as request routing and model selection, making reliable decisions critical to system performance. Fallback options accommodate categories outside regular choices, enabling deferral to human experts or more capable models. While recent works have examined adversarial vulnerabilities in TDMs, their ability to follow fallback rules in non-adversarial settings remains underexplored. We introduce the Paired Fallback Robustness (PFR) Test to evaluate two aspects of fallback reliability: whether models correctly switch between regular and fallback options, and whether they make consistent decisions under logically equivalent definitions of the same rule. We evaluate open-source decision models on three benchmarks, with controlled comparisons across architectures and parameter counts. We find that correct recognition does not reliably transfer to correct fallback options, and errors persist even when the correct category is explicitly supplied.Moreover, logically equivalent formulations of the same fallback rule can also produce substantial disagreement in model decisions. These findings reveal a crucial reliability gap in current TDMs: fallback mechanisms designed to improve reliability can instead introduce errors. It highlights faithful execution of fallback rules and consistency under equivalent definitions as essential requirements for reliable typed decision-making.

papers.title: Energy Consumption Analysis of Discrete Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models
papers.translated_title: Energy Consumption Analysis of Discrete Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models
papers.author: Boris Ruf
papers.summary: As Large Language Models (LLMs) continue to scale, their energy consumption during inference has become a critical concern. While Autoregressive (AR) models are the industry standard, Diffusion Language Models (DLLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative capable of parallel token generation. In this paper, we perform a comparative energy benchmark of diffusion models (LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B) against AR counterparts (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B). We analyze the trade-offs between model architecture, KV-cache optimization, and Joules-per-token efficiency. Our results show that at longer sequences (200--600 tokens), diffusion models achieve 2.5--2.7 J/token, approximately 2$\times$ more efficient than AR models with KV-cache (5.3--5.7 J/token). KV-cache provides substantial benefits for AR models at longer sequences (50--70\% energy reduction).

papers.title: DeltaStreamer: Towards Human-Like Agentic Streaming Video Understanding
papers.translated_title: DeltaStreamer: Towards Human-Like Agentic Streaming Video Understanding
papers.author: Boyuan Sun
papers.summary: We propose DeltaStreamer, a novel agentic framework for streaming video understanding inspired by how humans observe, remember, and investigate. Streaming video understanding requires a system to retain evidence before knowing which details future queries will need. Existing approaches often obscure event transitions and omit relevant details when compressing video history, and cannot recover missing visual evidence. DeltaStreamer addresses these limitations by combining change-aware memory with query-driven planning and targeted evidence gathering with replay. Before a query arrives, it continuously observes the stream and explicitly records visual changes in structured memory, preserving how events unfold rather than only what is present. When a query arrives, a query-driven planner identifies the required evidence and guides memory retrieval and targeted replay. By revisiting historical frames, the agent can recover visual details omitted during observation and ground its answer in evidence beyond the retained descriptions. This connects continuous observation with active investigation tailored to each question. Experiments on OVO-Bench and StreamingBench demonstrate improvements over representative streaming video understanding methods, with overall scores of 66.07% and 59.53%, respectively. Project page: https://bbbbchan.github.io/DeltaStreamer/

papers.title: OpenTWBench (Open Taiwan Benchmark): Taiwan-Domain Knowledge Evaluation for Large Language Models, and How the Measurement Apparatus Shapes the Score
papers.translated_title: OpenTWBench (Open Taiwan Benchmark): Taiwan-Domain Knowledge Evaluation for Large Language Models, and How the Measurement Apparatus Shapes the Score
papers.author: Liang-Hsun Huang
papers.summary: We present OpenTWBench, an open evaluation suite for Taiwan-domain knowledge in large language models, built around two benchmarks. tw-exam-bench contains 255,854 four-option questions across 148 academic subjects, from fifteen years of Taiwan's national examinations published as open data by the Ministry of Examination; answer keys agree across 31,312 duplicated question groups at 99.91%, with all 27 disagreements accounted for. A reviewed second pass withdrew 2,180 items whose stems depend on a figure the text does not carry; all scores use the remaining 253,674. tw-formosa-bench contains 1,696 difficulty-curated questions about everyday and contemporary Taiwan - the Taiwan that licensing examinations never ask about - generated from a community-curated corpus under a discipline in which no model writes a ground truth, and curated against a frozen seven-model pool so that the pool scored at the passing margin (46.9-74.6%, median ~54%); a leave-one-out experiment shows the selection preserves model ranking (near-zero bias). Within six weeks the frontier had cleared that band: of 108 models now on the public board, 22 score above its ceiling, the best 91.6%. We also document how much of a score comes from the apparatus rather than the model. On identical questions, switching answer extraction from pattern matching to an explicit \boxed{} answer moves accuracy from 20.8% to 93.9%; a single placeholder character in a system prompt moved one model from last (58.2%) to first (83.9%) on the same benchmark; doubling the thinking budget from 8k to 16k tokens bought 0.2% while shuffling which questions failed; and a three-judge validation panel proved to be one judge in disguise, two members approving 92-99% of everything shown. We release all datasets, per-item difficulty data, curation manifests and a leaderboard at https://opentwbench.ai

papers.title: VisibilitySplat: Ray-Traced Occlusion for Relighting with 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.translated_title: VisibilitySplat: Ray-Traced Occlusion for Relighting with 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.author: Sven Kluge
papers.summary: We address inverse rendering with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) by introducing explicit visibility modeling for relighting as well as material and light decomposition. Our approach augments the standard rasterized 3DGS pipeline with a sparse visibility oracle that estimates transmittance-weighted occlusion for Gaussian primitives from sampled lighting directions. This oracle is implemented using a point-based ray tracer accelerated by a bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) and queried sparsely within the inverse-rendering objectives, while the original 3DGS loop is retained for training efficiency, interactive visualization, and tooling compatibility. Shading follows a physically based rendering (PBR) formulation with a principled microfacet bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) and low-resolution high-dynamic-range (HDR) environment maps. We evaluate our method on the TensoIR synthetic dataset against baselines based on neural radiance fields (NeRFs), tensor representations, and 3DGS. The results show competitive performance and improvements over several earlier baselines for novel-view synthesis (NVS), albedo reconstruction, and relighting. Ablations indicate that explicit visibility modeling is an important contributor to relighting and material-illumination disentanglement, while pure PBR supervision can favor appearance fitting in NVS. Overall, the findings suggest that sparse, point-based visibility queries effectively complement rasterized splatting for inverse rendering while preserving the practical advantages of the 3DGS ecosystem.

papers.title: Early dopamine elevation modifies the behavioral consequences of maternal separation in female and male juvenile mice
papers.translated_title: Early dopamine elevation modifies the behavioral consequences of maternal separation in female and male juvenile mice
papers.author: Reis, A. L. d. A. L.
papers.summary: Alterations in dopaminergic signaling and exposure to early-life stress are both implicated in the developmental origins of psychiatric disorders, yet little is known about how these factors interact during sensitive periods of brain maturation. We investigated whether increased dopamine availability during early postnatal development modifies the behavioral consequences of maternal separation in female and male C57BL/6 mice. From postnatal day (PD) 1 to PD14, mice received L-Dopa plus benserazide, maternal separation (3 h/day), their combination, or the corresponding control conditions. We assessed mice behavior between PD28 and PD32 using novel object recognition, open-field, elevated plus-maze, marble-burying, and forced-swim tests, followed by hippocampal volumetric analysis. Early L-Dopa exposure produced sex- and behavior-specific effects. In females, L-Dopa increased rearing without altering horizontal locomotion and modified open-arm exploration and stress-coping behavior, whereas in males it increased open-arm exploration and reduced climbing frequency. Maternal separation produced distinct effects in females and males and reduced repetitive digging/burying behavior in both sexes. Importantly, maternal separation frequently modified rather than potentiated the effects of L-Dopa. In both sexes, combined maternal separation and L-Dopa opposed several L-Dopa-associated alterations in open-field, elevated plus-maze, and forced-swim behaviors. Recognition memory was largely preserved across experimental conditions. L-Dopa also reduced hippocampal volume selectively in females, whereas hippocampal volume was higher in females exposed to maternal separation plus L-Dopa than in those receiving L-Dopa alone. Multivariate analyses revealed overlapping rather than treatment-specific behavioral clusters, indicating substantial individual heterogeneity and sex-dependent shifts in multidimensional behavioral profiles. Together, these findings demonstrate that transient alterations in dopamine availability and maternal separation interact non-additively during early postnatal development. Their consequences depend on sex, behavioral domain, and developmental timing, supporting a model in which neurochemical and environmental perturbations dynamically shape behavioral trajectories rather than simply producing cumulative developmental damage.

papers.title: Spontaneous Hemodynamic Oscillations during Sleep Coordinate Directional CSF Flow in the Subarachnoid Space and Ventricles
papers.translated_title: Spontaneous Hemodynamic Oscillations during Sleep Coordinate Directional CSF Flow in the Subarachnoid Space and Ventricles
papers.author: Chen, D.
papers.summary: During sleep, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow is enhanced and thought to facilitate clearance of metabolic waste from the brain. Human imaging has shown that sleep is associated with large waves of bulk CSF flow in the fourth ventricle; however, the CSF flow dynamics around brain tissue are unknown. Here, we investigated how CSF flow is organized across the subarachnoid space, a key site both for fluid exchange across cortical surface and for transport out of the cranium. We used an MRI technology at 7 Tesla that simultaneously measures cortical hemodynamics and slow subarachnoid CSF flow and applied this during sleep. We found that spontaneous infraslow hemodynamic oscillations were coupled to spatially structured, directional CSF flow throughout both ventricular and subarachnoid compartments. Hemodynamic oscillations and fourth-ventricle bulk flow were both associated with brain-wide CSF flow at different phases, indicating that they reflect a single coordinated CSF movement cycle. Compared to cardiac pulsations, a canonical driver of CSF movement, hemodynamic-driven CSF flow showed a distinct directional pattern and was smaller in instantaneous amplitude but produced substantially greater cumulative displacement and thus greater potential for transport within an oscillation period. Together, these findings show that hemodynamic oscillations during sleep are coupled to temporally coordinated and directional CSF flow throughout the ventricles and subarachnoid space, suggesting that sleep-dependent neuronal activity drives fluid movement across the human brain in a distinct spatial pattern.

papers.title: Co-option of CENP-A for activity-induced neuronal plasticity
papers.translated_title: Co-option of CENP-A for activity-induced neuronal plasticity
papers.author: Stankovic, A.
papers.summary: Neuronal activation drives activity-dependent gene expression that underlies experience-associated synaptic modifications, learning and memory. Here we show that the histone variant CENP-A, best known for specifying centromere identity, is dynamically regulated by synaptic activity at both the RNA and protein levels in postmitotic neurons. Neuronal activation increases a non-centromeric nuclear pool of CENP-A while leaving centromeric CENP-A levels unchanged. Downregulation of CENP-A selectively reduces the activity-associated non-centromeric pool, impairs activity-dependent induction of immediate-early genes such as FOS and ARC, and disrupts hippocampus-dependent learning and memory. Furthermore, we find that activity-dependent neuronal responses in human embryonic stem cell-derived forebrain organoids similarly require CENP-A. Our results reveal a mitosis-independent, conserved role of CENP-A for driving plasticity in mammalian neurons.

papers.summary: Tick-borne diseases are reported across much of Illinois, yet tick surveillance remains spatially uneven, leaving many counties with limited species-specific observations. Relative abundance was defined as the species-specific share of the collected focal ticks and modeled using beta-binomial models that incorporated climate, land cover, forest fragmentation, deer habitat suitability, and BYM2 spatial effects in INLA. Statewide predictions extended inference to counties lacking species-specific observations and identified where uncertainty remained greatest, providing a basis for prioritizing additional surveillance across Illinois.

papers.summary: Urbanization is an accelerating evolutionary force, yet the patterns and drivers of urban gene flow remain largely obscured. Consequently, urban demographic sinks can simultaneously act as vital genetic bridges. Our findings reject a pure urban fragmentation model while demonstrating that demographic sink dynamics and genetic facilitation are not mutually exclusive. This demonstrates that high-turnover urban sinks can buffer regional biodiversity against genetic erosion, highlighting the need to prioritize matrix permeability and inter-patch connectivity in urban conservation strategies.

papers.summary: Whilst forms of non-associative learning such as habituation are widely reported in single-celled organisms, whether associative learning is possible in systems without a nervous system is contested. In this study, we implemented a conditioning paradigm in the acellular slime mould Physarum polycephalum through repeated pairings of nutrients with an aversive blue light stimulus. We first established that blue light is aversive under our conditioning protocol, slowing migration and producing broader, less directed growth, confirming its well documented effect on behaviour. Subjects were then trained in up to four training sessions by placing an oat stimulus inside a region with blue light before testing with the light presented alone. Trained subjects were more likely to reach the blue light region compared to untrained controls, with shorter latency, suggesting that Physarum weakens its avoidance of blue light after the region has repeatedly coincided with a nutrient. We conclude that a history of co-presentation is sufficient to relax an aversive response in Physarum but cannot, within the present study, attribute that change to associative learning.

Thus, these observations provide insights into the mechanisms of ribosome dormancy in the absence of FMRP and in understanding the role of rRNA methylation in translational regulation.

Together, these findings identify how pulsatile pressure within microvessels can generate directional interstitial fluid transport and enhance solute clearance, potentially contributing to tissue homeostasis.

papers.summary: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) coupled with Dorado modification-aware basecalling enables mapping of epitranscriptomic modifications including N6-methyladenosine (m6A) at the level of individual RNAs. papers.author: Brusseau, M.
papers.summary: BACKGROUND: Older adults with cancer often struggle to achieve recommended levels of physical activity and dietary intake. Ecological momentary assessment combined with accelerometry can provide insights into the temporal dynamics of psychological and behavioral processes at the individual level, such as motivation towards health behaviors. OBJECTIVE: This N-of-1 study aims to improve physical activity and dietary intake among older patients with cancer using an mHealth behavioral intervention. METHODS: A single-subject ABA' design will be employed among older patients with cancer ([≥] 70 years). A 2-week baseline phase (A) will be followed by an 8-week intervention phase (B) and a 2-week follow-up phase (A'). Throughout all these phases, participants will complete a daily data collection protocol combining ecological momentary assessment questionnaires and an ActiGraph wGT3X-BT accelerometer worn on the waist to measure physical activity. Ecological momentary assessment questionnaires will be delivered via a digital application to collect information on dietary intake, fatigue, and motivational constructs based on the Theory of Planned Behavior. The intervention (B) will consist of an mHealth intervention based on behavior change techniques, delivered via weekly calls, personalized messages, and a digital application. Data will be analyzed using piecewise regression models. In addition, a semi-structured interview will be conducted to assess patient experience. These qualitative data will help identify contextual factors, such as treatment-related side effects or variations in health status, that may have influenced behavior change and participation in data collection. CONCLUSION: This N-of-1 study explores intra-individual behavioral dynamics using intensive longitudinal data rather than testing a strictly reversible intervention effect. The mHealth intervention is based on behavior change techniques, with adjustments tailored to participants' progress and changing circumstances. The results will contribute to the evidence base for mHealth interventions designed to promote sustained physical activity and dietary intake among older adults with cancer.

Twenty-six curated benign/likely benign and 30 curated pathogenic/likely pathogenic missense variants were expressed in Flp-In HEK293 cells with CACNB4 and CACNA2D1. papers.title: Genome-wide association and Mendelian randomization analyses of host response to Helicobacter pylori infection implicate HLA polymorphisms and immune-mediated diseases.
papers.translated_title: Genome-wide association and Mendelian randomization analyses of host response to Helicobacter pylori infection implicate HLA polymorphisms and immune-mediated diseases.
papers.author: Kyosaka, T.
papers.summary: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infects the gastric epithelium of approximately half of the global population, and is a well-known risk factor for developing gastric cancer. Despite the clinical significance of H. pylori infection, many genetic factors underlying host response to H. pylori remain unidentified. Moreover, although H. pylori infection has been implicated in a range of extra-gastric diseases, whether these associations share a common genetic architecture remains unclear. papers.title: Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for Wound Management: Clinical Evidence, Energy Delivery Parameters and Mechanistic Insights - A Systematic Review
papers.translated_title: Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for Wound Management: Clinical Evidence, Energy Delivery Parameters and Mechanistic Insights - A Systematic Review
papers.author: Musolf, B. M.
papers.summary: Background/Objectives: Chronic wounds such as diabetic foot ulcers, venous leg ul-cers and burns are a major health-care burden. Extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) is a non-invasive treatment that promotes angiogenesis and tissue regenera-tion. This review synthesizes the clinical evidence for ESWT in wound management, and asks how contemporary reviews reflect it. Methods: PubMed and Ovid/Embase were searched from inception to 1 September 2026 according to PRISMA, regardless of wound type, study design or ESWT modality. Fifty-one clinical studies and 46 prior re-views were analyzed. Heterogeneity confined the primary synthesis to a qualitative one; an exploratory pooled analysis was performed for the one endpoint reported con-sistently enough to permit it. Results: None of the 46 previously published reviews covered the original evidence in its full breadth: each cited a median of 19.4% of the clinical studies available at its reference date (range 0-90.9%), and systematic reviews covered no more than narrative ones. Most studies reported improved healing across all four modalities. In seven controlled trials reporting complete healing as events and denominators, the pooled risk ratio favored ESWT (1.51, 95% CI 1.22-1.87; I2 = 0%; 689 patients). Such data existed for three modalities only, resting on one trial for two, so modalities could not be compared. Conclusions: ESWT is a useful adjunct for acute and chronic wounds. Because no previous review reflected the evidence base as a whole, conclusions drawn from it should be read with caution. Head-to-head trials with matched physical dose are needed before any modality can be preferred.

papers.title: Haploinsufficiency, de novo and biallelic missense variants in CSMD2 are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders
papers.translated_title: Haploinsufficiency, de novo and biallelic missense variants in CSMD2 are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders
papers.author: Pailler-Pradeau, C.
papers.summary: CUB and Sushi domains-containing CSMD proteins are involved in neuron development. Variants in the CSMD1-3 paralogs were GWAS-associated with cognition, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), schizophrenia and brain structure, suggesting that these genes could be linked to neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD). Indeed, rare biallelic variants in all three CSMD paralogs were recently associated with epilepsy, while rare biallelic variants in CSMD1 were also linked with intellectual disability and cortical malformations. We identified nine individuals from eight families carrying CSMD2 biallelic missense variants in developmental delay/intellectual disability cohorts. Affected individuals presented with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD and brain anomalies. Consistent with gnomAD metrics that suggest CSMD2 haploinsufficiency, we also report two families segregating monoallelic CSMD2 frameshift variants, which complement a described de novo truncation variant in an ASD proband. We concomitantly report two phenotypically overlapping individuals with de novo CSMD2 missense variants and compare them to twelve de novo CSMD2 cases identified in published trio analyses. UK Biobank analyses showed nominally significant enrichment of ADHD, ASD and neuroticism in volunteers carrying at least one rare CSMD2 variant. In silico modelling and immunofluorescence assays showed that mutated residues in affected individuals with biallelic and de novo missense variants are clustering in two regions and that the encoded proteins showed impaired membrane localization and an increased cytoplasmic aggregation. Zebrafish crispant larvae for the orthologous csmd2 presented with microcephaly, smaller cerebellum, and reduced Purkinje cell size. Larvae also displayed decreased swimming velocity, diminished connectivity between the optic tecta, and abnormal peripheral neuronal branching. We demonstrate that rare, likely pathogenic variants in CSMD2 are associated with both autosomal recessive and dominant forms of NDD further substantiating the functional significance of CSMD paralogs in neurogenesis/synapse formation.

papers.title: A Growing Burden, a Persistent Gap: Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome Education and Emergency Department Trends in Michigans Legal Cannabis Market
papers.translated_title: A Growing Burden, a Persistent Gap: Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome Education and Emergency Department Trends in Michigans Legal Cannabis Market
papers.author: Lorbeer, E. R.
papers.summary: Background: Since Michigan's legalization of recreational adult-use cannabis in December 2018, health care providers in the city of Kalamazoo, Michigan, have informally observed an increase in cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome (CHS) presentations, although the extent of this increase has not been formally characterized locally. CHS is frequently underrecognized and misdiagnosed, often resulting in repeated emergency department (ED) visits and substantial diagnostic costs before a diagnosis is reached. Despite this clinical and financial burden, it is unclear whether consumers are adequately informed of this risk through point-of-sale or public health resources. Methods: A cross-sectional environmental scan was conducted to identify publicly available educational content about CHS on the websites of licensed cannabis retailers in Kalamazoo and relevant public health agencies. Provisioning centers and public health websites were screened using a structured coding rubric developed specifically for the environmental scan to assess the presence, depth, web page placement, and intended audience of CHS-related content. Additionally, the electronic medical records at a local teaching hospital in Kalamazoo were queried to identify ED visits with a primary diagnosis of CHS from January 1, 2010 to December 31, 2025. Results: Before the legalization of marijuana, the hospital recorded six ED encounters with the primary diagnosis of CHS between January 2010 and November 2018, and 274 ED encounters between December 2018 and December 2025 (mean age: 29 years; 157 females, 123 males). The incidence rate of CHS-related ED encounters was 57.2 times higher during the post-legalization period than during the pre-legalization period (95% CI, 26.0-157.3; exact Poisson rate-ratio test, p < 0.0001). Among the licensed Kalamazoo provisioning centers reviewed, only one mentioned CHS as a warning but did not describe symptoms or offer medical guidance. CHS content was not identified on the websites of the state or local health departments. Conclusion: Despite the growing clinical concern regarding CHS, consumer-facing educational resources remain scarce. Although this study cannot establish a causal relationship between the availability of CHS-related educational content and the observed increase in ED encounters following legalization, it identifies a substantial lack of CHS-specific warnings in the evaluated consumer-facing resources. Given the clinical and potential economic burden associated with delayed CHS recognition, we recommend that Michigans existing point-of-sale pamphlet requirement be amended to include CHS-specific warning language.

papers.title: OSS-DBS v2: Simulation Platform for Biophysical Modelling of Deep Brain Stimulation
papers.translated_title: OSS-DBS v2: Simulation Platform for Biophysical Modelling of Deep Brain Stimulation
papers.author: Zimmermann, J.
papers.summary: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is a well-established therapy for various neurological disorders. Clinical outcomes of DBS depend on electrode placement and stimulation programming, with growing evidence suggesting that targeting specific sites and networks can improve therapeutic efficacy. This targeting can be facilitated using high-accuracy, multi-modal biophysical models. In this article, we present the open-source platform OSS-DBS v2 that enables researchers and clinicians to build such biophys- ical models. Building upon previous work, the new version combines automated volume conductor generation, accurate and efficient electric field modelling and stimulation-driven neural simulations. OSS-DBS v2 provides an extensive library of intracranial electrodes, which can be modelled simul- taneously to test complex stimulation paradigms. Its application programming interface facilitates integration of external data workflows, such as impedance measurements. Furthermore, an integration with the Lead-DBS toolbox offered a straightforward graphical user interface for stimulation volume and pathway activation modelling, further complemented by an optimization framework. OSS-DBS v2 relies entirely on open-source software, supports all major operating systems and is designed for efficient execution on consumer-grade hardware.
